inspected.finding: First creation generates a new installation identity; ordinary cancellation/resume/reconfiguration keeps identity and history. Saved READY is not activation. No separately confirmed reset/replacement workflow exists here.
Native binding, revision, parent image, staging/promotion and exact readback provide reusable protected-state primitives. Generic pending promotion alone is not a reset safety or authority proof.
Resolver revocation is installation-bound local metadata, not deletion or remote revocation of the underlying key and not by itself a durable reset transaction.

Protected images retain selections/bindings and may only gain revocation; fresh restore preserves revoked status. A reset must retain required evidence and revoke only owned references without copying another installation's credentials.

Current owner-controlled REVOKE preserves the catalogue/profile and increases its revision. REGISTER with any previous binding is deliberately refused; there is no controlled new-installation replacement mode. Lost replies inspect exact pending after-image. Existing revocation may preserve unresolved work; it is not proof that full reset may discard it.

A distinct installation and approved target are required; initial selection refuses any existing binding. Shared revocation inspection is supported; fresh reenrollment after reset needs a separately qualified transition.

Current actor/name enrollment is static in each instance. Stale/forced takeover is immediate conditional acquisition; old grants lose current ownership. Permanent reset retirement is not established by an epoch change alone and needs a fresh qualified guard without peer/old-host ACK.

Role election and fresh ordinary dispatch use capability/current owner checks; local maintenance holds work. A reset must integrate its retirement/quiescence guard at actual boundaries, not rely on a saved UI flag.

Existing typed snapshots retain shared BUSY/UNREAD/UNKNOWN, setup pending/UNKNOWN, election/mutation and effect evidence. Safe summaries expose fixed counts, not identities. Reset-specific scope and current facts still need qualification.
Current-role and explicit zero-blocker proof are reusable for controlled coordination; reset must preserve immediate takeover independently.
Reconfiguration deliberately retains installation identity, nonce, operation history and original archive. It must not silently become a full reset.

required_invariants: An owner selects the exact local installation/role and sees irreversible identity/enrollment/reference consequences before explicit confirmation; no implied reset of peers, shared network or root.
Full reset preserves required original/pending/work evidence and refuses unsafe unread/unknown effects. An existing low-level revoke/cancel call is not a quiescence certificate.
Revoke only this installation's scoped references/enrollment; no unrelated secret deletion or copied fallback identity.
Old cooperative processes must fail fresh retirement/identity/epoch checks before new actions after reenrollment. A cached profile, old grant or zero-blocker UI view cannot grant execution.
Partial/unknown reset effects are inspected as the same operation; no blind replay or generation rollback. Irreversible revocation cannot be undone by restoring an old profile.
Fresh commissioning collects facts and produces a distinct installation identity while retaining the same canonical shared objects/work/history; no whole-root deletion.
Stale/forced WATCHDOG first-CAS takeover remains available without an old-host or all-peer acknowledgement barrier.

next_bounded_unit.purpose: A deterministic nonmutating review of the selected own WATCHDOG or FETCHER installation, with fixed consequence/prerequisite wording and a private current-profile binding for later explicit confirmation.
negative_checks: Private identity, paths, reference or provider-canary leakage
next_bounded_unit.boundaries: No reset executor, shared mutation, credential use/revocation, local identity replacement, GUI activation or network/provider operation. Any implementation must first have a separate published/read-back INTENT and linked scope amendment. This unit alone accepts no C1-C4 check.

remaining_work: Complete reset transaction/owned binding and role retirement, actual native state and current shared proof, interrupted/unknown recovery, old-process refusal, controlled FETCHER replacement and fresh first-run composition; then original C1-C4/common platform/privacy/rollback acceptance. Full GUI integration follows its canonical plan scope.

owner_pause.reason: Owner asked to stop at a completed resumable work boundary and briefly report this run.
owner_pause.next_action: Wait for the owner's explicit continue. Then read this checkpoint and publish a new RP028.C1 INTENT for the smallest nonmutating reset-review unit: exact own-role scope, deterministic consequence/prerequisite summary and stale/cross-installation/secret-leakage refusal tests. First record its linked amendment; later units must qualify retirement fencing, protected evidence, partial-reset recovery and fresh reenrollment before any RP028 check is accepted.
